what: Users want a proper app/player for music purchased on Bandcamp so they can listen seamlessly without falling back to Spotify/YouTube or limited local file apps. DTC model fails on everyday playback UX.
why_us: High engagement (369+ likes on wish, 490 on original complaint) shows clear demand for better local/owned music consumption tools; niche but passionate users.
revenue: Potential subscription or freemium for offline/local music library manager

what: Indie app developer hit $600 MRR on a new app that is now on autopilot (no changes for over a month), only weekly + annual subscriptions, still growing. Part of larger portfolio strategy.
why_us: Concrete numbers + 347 likes; shows replicable micro-app model with low maintenance after launch. High payment willingness via subscriptions.

what: Homy.app (Mac file organizer / digital home) launched: 2.6k visitors, 83 licenses sold, $786 revenue in first 24 hours. Extending limited slots.
why_us: Fast validation of AI-adjacent productivity tool with real revenue on day 1; TrustMRR proof mentioned. Shows demand for clean, cute local-first organizers.

what: If software lacks an easy text box for feature requests that appear quickly, users will just get Claude to replace the product entirely. Frustration with slow/no feedback loops.
why_us: 613 likes on clear statement of switching to AI agents for missing features. Strong signal that tools without rapid AI-assisted customization or feedback will lose users.
revenue: N/A (pain point for existing SaaS; opportunity for AI integration layers)

what: Lovable.dev (AI app builder) 1-star reviews: credits burned on repeated AI errors, failed publishes, almost zero real support (only AI bot), projects lost, waste of money.
why_us: Repeated complaints about reliability, cost opacity, and support in popular AI wrapper category. Opportunity for more transparent/reliable AI coding tools or credit management.

what: Curated list of 23 free open-source GitHub tools/repos for memecoin traders (wallet trackers, rug checkers, AI agents, backtesters) instead of paid bots. High bookmark engagement.
why_us: 273 likes + 466 bookmarks shows demand for free/open alternatives to expensive trading bots; opportunity for better packaged automation or freemium tools.
revenue: Paid bots exist; free alternatives popular

what: Notion Trustpilot complaints: misleading free tier then sudden charges/extra credits for AI, hidden fees, difficult account management, support issues.
why_us: Subscription fatigue + opaque AI credit pricing is a recurring pain across productivity tools. Clear willingness to switch if better pricing/transparency.
revenue: Users paying €200/mo then needing more credits
